headline_marked: Police disperse [[protest against NCT deal with DP World]] in Dhaka
headline: Police disperse protest against NCT deal with DP World in Dhaka
summary: Left-leaning political and labour organisations marched on Invest Bangladesh office, claiming the 15-year lease of the container terminal to a UAE firm is a 'suicidal decision'.
details: Police dispersed a protest in Dhaka’s Agargaon today against the government’s decision to lease the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) at Chattogram port to UAE-based DP World.

The protest was organised by the Anti-Imperialism and Anti-War Alliance, along with several left-leaning political and labour organisations, who marched from Agargaon metro rail station to the Invest Bangladesh office.
The Democratic Rights Committee reported that several people were injured when police baton-charged protesters, though the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station OC denied that batons were used.
Protesters claimed that handing over the container terminal to a foreign company poses a threat to national security, economic independence, and sovereignty, calling the move a 'suicidal decision'.
The protesters alleged that the deal began under the Awami League government and was accelerated by the interim government, with the final agreement signed today despite continued opposition.
Bangladesh has now officially signed a 15-year concession agreement with DP World to operate and maintain the NCT and its overflow container yard at Chattogram port.
caption:
A 15-year deal to hand over a port terminal to a UAE firm sparks protests in Dhaka, leading to clashes with police.

Police dispersed a protest in Dhaka’s Agargaon today against the government’s decision to lease the New Mooring Container Terminal (NCT) at Chattogram port to UAE-based DP World.

The protest was organised by the Anti-Imperialism and Anti-War Alliance, along with several left-leaning political and labour organisations, who marched from Agargaon metro rail station to the Invest Bangladesh office.

The Democratic Rights Committee reported that several people were injured when police baton-charged protesters, though the Sher-e-Bangla Nagar Police Station OC denied that batons were used.

Protesters claimed that handing over the container terminal to a foreign company poses a threat to national security, economic independence, and sovereignty, calling the move a 'suicidal decision'.

The protesters alleged that the deal began under the Awami League government and was accelerated by the interim government, with the final agreement signed today despite continued opposition.

Bangladesh has now officially signed a 15-year concession agreement with DP World to operate and maintain the NCT and its overflow container yard at Chattogram port.

caption:
1,935 people hospitalised in just 24 hours. Dengue continues to claim lives across Bangladesh.

Five more patients have died of dengue and 1,935 others were hospitalised in the last 24 hours, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).

This brings the total death toll for the year to 294, with 49 of those deaths occurring in the first eight days of October.

September was the deadliest month of the year so far, recording 148 deaths and 43,774 hospitalisations.

In the last 24 hours, 175 patients were admitted to hospitals in Dhaka North and 233 in Dhaka South, while 382 more were admitted across the Dhaka Division.

Other divisions reported significant numbers: Chattogram (280), Khulna (292), Rajshahi (206), Barishal (195), Mymensingh (93), Rangpur (64), and Sylhet (15).

A total of 2,057 dengue patients were discharged from hospitals during the same period.

Overall, 94,151 patients have been hospitalised this year, with 88,208 recovering and leaving the hospitals.
